1. Allowed, subject to all just exceptions.
2. Petitioners seek quashing of FIR No.1078/2018 of PS Mangolpuri for the offences under Section 498A/406/34 IPC and the proceedings arising out of the same.
Quashing of the FIR is sought by petitioners on the ground that they have compromised all disputes with complainant de facto (respondent no.2 herein).
Petitioner no.1 and respondent no.2 have appeared in person, identified by their respective counsel and Investigating Officer/SI Manita.
3. I spoke with respondent no.2 in Hindi.
4. Respondent no.2 submitted that she wants to continue her matrimony This is a digitally signed order.

The Order is downloaded from the DHC Server on 27/06/2025 at 22:39:48 with the petitioner no.1.
On being pointed out the decree of divorce (pdf page 91), respondent no.2 submits that she is not aware if the marriage between her and petitioner no.1 stands dissolved by decree of divorce.

Further, respondent no.2 submits that before the divorce court, she was not asked anything and was only made to sign some document, after which someone said that the divorce petition is pending while someone said that the divorce has already been granted.

Even as regards statement recorded by the Joint Registrar (Judicial) on 22.05.2025, respondent no.2 stated that nothing was asked from her and the Presiding Officer only directed the stenographer to record her statement, after which the stenographer told her that the statement had already been typed and is just to be signed by her.

sentences.text: A duly sworn Hindi affidavit of respondent no.2 be filed as regards the aforesaid within two weeks.
At this stage, respondent no.2 submits that she is completely illiterate and cannot read even Hindi or any other language.

Therefore, it is directed that the Oath Commissioner before whom she testifies in Hindi shall make specific certification on the affidavit that the contents thereof have been read over and explained to respondent no.2 and she admits the same to be correct.
Till next date, the trial court proceedings shall remain stayed in view of the aforesaid.
GIRISH KATHPALIA, J MAY 28, 2025/ry
